description: This chart presents three pie charts, labeled "easy," "medium," and "hard," each depicting the distribution of four categories—N+K+, N−K+, N−K−, and N+K−—under a "Zero-Shot" evaluation. Each pie chart contains four colored segments: teal for N+K+, yellow for N−K+, orange for N−K−, and red for N+K−. The "easy" chart shows teal (N+K+) at 55.4%, yellow (N−K+) at 38.3%, orange (N−K−) at 4.6%, and red (N+K−) at 1.7%. The "medium" chart shows teal (N+K+) at 58.8%, yellow (N−K+) at 35.4%, orange (N−K−) at 4.8%, and red (N+K−) at 1.8%. The "hard" chart shows teal (N+K+) at 18.1%, yellow (N−K+) at 37.3%, orange (N−K−) at 37.9%, and red (N+K−) at 6.7%. All percentage values are labeled directly within their respective slices, and a legend on the right confirms the color-to-category mapping. The slices are not exploded or otherwise visually emphasized, and while the segments appear ordered by descending size within each pie chart, no explicit ordering is indicated across the charts.
